title: Root-First Tree Walk
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree. Walk it depth-first so that every node is listed before anything in its subtrees, and its whole left subtree is listed before its right subtree.

Return the node values in that order. An empty tree gives an empty list.

examples.why: 8 first, then all of its left subtree (3, 1, 6), and only then the right subtree (10, 14).
5 has no left child. 9 is its right child, and 7 is 9's left child.

hints: Write down what has to happen at one node: the node itself, then the left side, then the right side.
Recursion does exactly that in three lines. Can you do it without recursion, so a 10 000-deep chain cannot overflow the call stack?
Use an explicit stack. Pop a node, record it, then push its right child and then its left child, so the left one comes off first.

explain.intuition:
Root-first order is the order a recursive function naturally produces if it records the node before recursing: record, go left, go right. It is the same order in which a browser would print the opening tags of a DOM tree.

To remove recursion, replace the call stack with your own. A stack is last-in, first-out, so after recording a node you push the right child first and the left child second. The left child then comes off next, and the whole left subtree is finished before the right child surfaces again.
steps: If the tree is empty, return an empty list.
Push the root on a stack.
While the stack is not empty: pop a node and append its value.
Push its right child (if any), then its left child (if any).
pitfalls: Pushing the left child before the right child. The stack then visits the right subtree first.
Recursing on a tree that is one long chain. Deep trees can overflow the call stack; the explicit stack has no such limit.
Appending the value after visiting the children. That is a different order (children first).

complexity.space: O(h) for the stack, h = tree height

solutions.title: Recursion
solutions.idea: Record the node, then recurse into the left subtree, then the right one.

solutions.title: Explicit stack
solutions.idea: Pop, record, push right then left. The left child is popped next, so left subtrees finish first.

followups: Produce the same order using O(1) extra space by temporarily rewiring right pointers (Morris traversal).
Turn the walk into a lazy iterator with a next() method that yields one value at a time.
